MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 9, 2020

Due to COVID-19 and the “Stay at Home” Order for the State of California and the Social
Distance Guidelines issued by Federal, State, and Local Authorities this Council Meeting was
conducted via Video Teleconferencing for all Council and Staff with the exception of the City
Attorney and City Clerk who were present in the Council Chamber. All public comments that
were emailed to the City Clerk were read during the meeting.

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Goodell
at 5:00 p.m., on June 9, 2020, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on June 5, 2020, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Teleconferenced:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Teleconferenced:  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services

Staff Present:  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel-Existing Litigation (Paragraph (1) of subdivision (d) of
  Section 54956.9) Name of case: Donaldson vs City of Mission Viejo.

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel: Existing Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph 4 of
  Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 - Southwest Voter Registration Education Project v.
  The City of Mission Viejo.
City Council Minutes  1  June 9, 2020
   Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Regarding CS2, she questioned the transparency of the City Council
  and asked why the withdrawal from the amicus brief on May 6, 2020, was not publicly
  disclosed.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:06 p.m., Mayor Goodell recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:11 p.m., with all five City Council Members present via teleconferencing.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council received an update on both Closed Session
items. The Council provided direction to staff but no reportable action occurred.

INVOCATION: Mayor Goodell

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Goodell read a statement, on behalf of the entire City Council, regarding the recent events
taking place in the Country, State and region.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Jose Trinidad Castaneda, III: Outlined the benefits of Community Choice Energy (CCE) and the
steps that can be taken to get started with the program.

Catherine Palmer, M.V.: Shared that the Irvine City Council has consensus to move forward on the
formation of a Joint Powers Authority (JPA) for new Community Choice Energy (CCE) programs.
She encouraged the City to work with other south Orange County cities on the implementation of
CCE for the residents of Mission Viejo.

Chad Kroeger: Suggested renaming the International Space Station the “Tom Cruise Space
Station.”

J.T. Parr: Proclaimed that Tom Cruise is the hero we need right now during the pandemic.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Asked the Council on why they did not publicly announce the withdrawal
from the voting rights amicus brief and suggested that perhaps a quid pro quo has taken place to
gain favor from the Secretary of State.

Joshua Baum, M.V. Stated that the lack of action taken by the City has failed to live up to the
Community of Character values. He noted that there has yet to be a single statement from City
leaders on the importance of black lives.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

City Council Minutes  2  June 9, 2020
 On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of June 9, 2020, as presented.

2.  Check Register Dated May 15, 2020 in the Amount of $399,595.86

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated May 22, 2020 in the Amount of $2,486,564.15

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for April 2020

  Received and filed.

5.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for April 2020

  Received and filed.

6.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for April 2020

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for April 2020

  Received and filed.

8.  Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - Ten Months Ended April 30, 2020

  Received and filed.

9.  Annual Routine Street Sweeping Services

  (1) Approved the Sixth Amendment with Sunset Property Services for the period of July 1,
  2020, through December 31, 2020, in the amount of $221,940.00 (2) authorized staff to issue
  a purchase order to Sunset Property Services for the period of July 1, 2020, through December
  31, 2020, in an amount not to exceed $221,940.00.

10. Amendment to Saddleback Valley Unified School District Youth Services Contract
  2019-2021 for Kids Factory Program
City Council Minutes  3  June 9, 2020
   Approved amendment to Saddleback Valley Unified School District Youth Services Contract
  to provide Kids Factory Program during the 2020/2021 school year and establish participant
  fee at $300 per year.

11. Annual Review of Residential and Commercial Integrated Waste Management Rates

  Adopted Resolution 20-15 Approving the Proposed Trash Rate Adjustments for Residential
  (2.7% increase from $16.95 to $17.41 per month for Single-Family Standard Cart Service),
  Commercial (2.9% increase), and Roll-Off (3.0% increase) Services Effective July 1, 2020.

12. Annual Weed Abatement Program for Parcels Under One Acre - Year 2020 - Phase 1

  (1) Adopted Resolution 20-16 Declaring that Certain Weeds, Rubbish, Refuse, and Dirt on
  Parcels Under One Acre Constitute Nuisances; Declaring the Intention of the City Council to
  Order the Abatement of Said Nuisances; and Fixing a Time and Place for Hearing Protests;
  (2) instructed the Public Services Department to mail a Notice to Destroy Weeds in
  accordance with Section 39566 of the Government Code; and (3) instructed the City Clerk to
  set the Public Hearing for August 25, 2020.

13. Agreement for Legal Services

  Approved agreement for legal services with Lozano Smith effective June 1, 2020.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

OLD BUSINESS

14. Extension of the Proclamation of a Local Emergency For COVD-19

  Emergency Operations Manager Paul Catsimanes presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to extend the
  Existing Proclamation of a Local Emergency Due to COVID-19 to July 14, 2020.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

15. Resolution Authorizing Execution and Delivery of an Equipment Lease Purchase
  Agreement and Approve Related Documents and Actions and Review of Proposed Cart
  Fee Rates for the Golf Cart Lease Replacement for the Casta Del Sol Golf Course

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

City Council Minutes  4  June 9, 2020
   Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 20-17 Authorizing Execution and Delivery of an Equipment Lease Purchase
  Agreement and Approve Related Documents and Actions; (2) authorize City staff to enter
  into a 60-month lease agreement with PNC Equipment Finance LLC (A20-10)with a principal
  amount not to exceed $450,000; (3) approve the 60-month lease agreement with PNC
  Equipment Finance LLC to form and terms and approve authorized City staff to sign the
  agreement upon final negotiations with PNC Equipment Finance LLC; (4) authorize City staff
  to sign the sales proposal with E-Z-GO Corporation Division of TEXTRON to initiate the
  order; and (5) approve the recommended cart lease rates and authorize City staff to implement
  new cart fee rates effective July 1, 2020.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

16. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Sachs.

17. Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Received report from Mayor Pro Tem Kelley and Council Member Bucknum.

18. Transportation Corridor Agency (TCA) Report

  Received report from Mayor Pro Tem Kelley.

STAFF REPORTS

19. Fiscal Year 2020-2021 Law Enforcement Agreement and Additional Special
  Enforcement Services Provided by the Orange County Sheriff’s Department

  Emergency Operations Manager Paul Catsimanes presented the staff report.

  Joe Silvey, M.V.: Gave various suggestions for the Law Enforcement agreement in light of
  recent events.

  Alexandra Holtz: asked the Council to reconsider the contract with the Orange County
  Sheriff’s Department and instead invest the proposed $21 million in community programs.

  The following requested the City of Mission Viejo to cut its ties with the Orange County
  Sheriff's Department and reallocate the entire $20 million Law Enforcement Services
  Agreement budget towards youth programs, increased mental health services, neighborhood
  infrastructures, childcare, and community outreach for those who need these services most:
  Arya Jemal, M.V.; Caroline Strother, M.V.; Leah Atkins, Galicia South; Amira Attia, M.V.;
City Council Minutes  5  June 9, 2020
   Sumaiya Abdeali, Canyon Crest; Stephanie Tsai, M.V.; Emerson Martin, Sunrise Ridge;
  Katherine Fahey, Canyon Crest; Emma Kocik, Wilderness Glen; Roxana Akbari, Canyon
  Estates; Matthew Helmuth, M.V.; Ava Shakib, Lake Forest; Liam Collins, Carballo; Rose
  Akbari, Canyon Crest; Jeri Klucas, M.V.; Nikki Namdar, M.V.; Tiffany Hy, M.V.; Arianna
  Ford, M.V.; Camilla Ford, M.V.; Susan Crockett, M.V.; Alexandra Zetterberg, M.V.; Grayson
  Gothard, Lake Forest; Kimia Akbari, Orange County; Nicole Tarantino, M.V.; Sarah
  Guillermo, Dana Point; Ciaro Weitzel, M.V.; Alison Hutchins, M.V.; Amie Larsen, Castile
  Neighborhood; Garrett Larsen, Castile Neighborhood; Aidan Jones, Aegean Heights; Tarek
  Ghalwash, M.V.; Sandra Trumbly, M.V.; Lisa McKeever, La Mancha Neighborhood; Hannah
  Loftus, Canyon Crest; Elizabeth Acosta, Aliso Viejo; and Alli Stanojkovic, Baja Finisterra
  Community.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to (1) to
  approve the FY 2020-21 Law Enforcement Services Agreement with the County of Orange
  (A20-11) with the stipulation to not eliminate one motor deputy but create a “Hybrid Motor
  Deputy” position that would serve as both a School Resource Officer and a Motor Deputy;
  and (2) approve funding in FY 2020-21 in the amount not to exceed $35,000 for overtime
  related to special enforcement services.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

20. Update regarding Entering into a Sub-recipient Contract with the County of Orange to
  Receive Pass-through Federal Funds to Reimburse Specified City COVID-19 Response
  Costs: Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act ("CARES") Funds

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg provided the update.

  The City Council received and filed the report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

21. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum thanked the Mayor for representing the City by attending one of the
peaceful protests this week. She asked about the opening of playgrounds and said she has observed
residents removing the tape from around the play structures. This application takes a lot of staff
time for something that is unenforceable and she noted, in contrast, that people are allowed to attend
protests where they are not social distancing but children can’t play in the playgrounds. She asked
staff for input and City Manager Wilberg explained that the State has specifically said playgrounds
City Council Minutes  6  June 9, 2020
 are not allowed to be open. Council Member Bucknum said that the State brings down many
mandates that are difficult to enforce and at some point, the City needs to make this decision by
watching the budget and utilizing staff time efficiently. City Manager Wilberg responded that
unfortunately, the Joint Powers Insurance Authority (JPIA) has advised that anything that opens
before the State guidelines allow will not be covered if there is a claim or lawsuit. Council Member
Bucknum said she would like to have the next Council Meeting in the Chamber and City Attorney
Curley responded that the meeting will be open to the public and social distancing guidelines will
be in place. Council Member Bucknum encouraged residents to continue to show grace and
humility to fellow citizens and to show the world the unification of Mission Viejo. She expressed
concern for the businesses in town and urged residents to shop in Mission Viejo. Lastly, she
congratulated the graduates of 2020 and gave a shout out to her uncle on his 75 th birthday.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths congratulated the Class of 2020 and thanked the Mission Viejo Rotary Club
for handing out $5,000 in scholarships to graduates of local schools.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs asked staff to look into the Community Choice Energy (CCE) program to
evaluate the pros and cons of joining. He asked his colleagues who are on the Southern California
Association of Government (SCAG) Boards if there has been any discussion that the spread of
coronavirus has a correlation with high-density areas. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley responded that yes,
the COVID-19 virus has spread much more in densely populated areas and the SCAG Regional
Housing Needs Allocations are going forward and will not be adjusted. She shared that she has not
heard of any policy discussions on the SCAG Board. Council Member Bucknum explained the
responsibility of SCAG and City Attorney Curley spoke about pending legislation to respond to
some of the density concerns as well as the COVID-19 issues that will override local zoning and
allow housing to be put into any commercial zone. Council Member Sachs discussed the turmoil
going on throughout the country in larger cities and he read from Sheriff Barnes’ letter regarding
excessive force. He concluded his comments by letting residents know that Mission Viejo is safe
because of the Orange County Sheriff’s Department and there is no need to be worried.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that she participated in Zoom Meetings with representatives
from Saddleback Church and Mission Viejo Community Services Manager Drew Fine. The Church
has provided free dinners for essential works, set up food pantries, and they are looking into the
idea of organizing a job fair once City facilities reopen. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley noted that blood
supplies are low due to the cancellation of some blood drives and therefore, the City will host a
drive, sponsored by Senator Pat Bates, on Thursday June 11 from 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. in the
Saddleback Room at City Hall. A second blood drive will be held June 22 from 12:00 p.m. to 6:00
p.m. in the Saddleback Room. She also announced that there is a Red Cross Blood Center in Laguna
Hills where residents can make an appointment in advance. She encouraged residents to support
local businesses and announced that a new Automobile Club of Southern California (AAA) office
opened up in the old Sports Chalet Center on Puerta Real off Crown Valley Parkway. Mayor Pro
Tem Kelley stated that she is very excited that city pools will be opening and that the City is doing
everything that the State and the County are allowing. She said it has been a challenging year with
everything that has happened; the tragic killing of George Floyd has disgusted and sickened
City Council Minutes  7  June 9, 2020
 everyone, along with the Santa Cruz Deputy that was shot and killed, and a black security guard at
the Homeland Security Office that was killed. She expressed her concern with all the tragedy in the
Country and said that she has been in a lot of prayer every day. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley quoted
from the Bible: “Love your neighbor as yourself” and the Golden Rule: “Treat other people the way
you want to be treated.” Finally, she said she hopes this is a time that people can really focus on
being kind to each other, loving one another, and standing up for what is right.

Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell thanked his colleagues on the Council for their thoughtful comments and passion
for the City at this difficult time. He mentioned that the “Rename the Casta del Sol Golf Course
Contest” is underway and he encouraged residents to participate. He announced that he and Council
Member Sachs sit on the Economic Development Committee and this week, they reviewed the
proposals for the Master Plan of the Casta del Sol Golf Course and will be conducting interviews
with the firms that submitted proposals. There were ten entries and three interviews will be
performed to ask questions, explore ideas on the different options, and discuss the community
engagement piece where the residents will be able to add input. Mayor Goodell noted that in his
prayer earlier, he mentioned being patient and kind and that there is a lot of pent up frustration in
people. The Council Members are hearing it from within and also outside of the community. Mayor
Goodell informed residents that staff has done a great job preparing for the reopening the City’s
pools. He also shared that the Orange County Mayors lobbied the Board of Supervisors to release
the small business grants and that he volunteered, on behalf of the Mayors, to write a letter to the
County and State asking to reopen pools just as they allowed for the reopening of golf courses and
tennis courts. He noted that 26 of the 34 Mayors signed the letter which was sent to the Board of
Supervisors and the County Health Officer last week. At a meeting Tuesday morning, the Board of
Supervisors ordered the County Health Officer to work with the State to get the pools opened as
quickly as possible. Mayor Goodell announced that he attended a small protest on the corner of La
Paz and Marguerite to show support to residents who wanted to express their hope that things will
change in this Country. He was disheartened to receive hate mail from some people who said he is
anti-sematic and against police officers. Lastly, Mayor Goodell announced that he had the pleasure
of helping in a thank you effort for healthcare workers by distributing a free TK Burger lunch for
the staff at Mission Hospital this week.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:14 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Goodell adjourned the meeting - in honor of the heroes that have put themselves in harm’s
way to keep the rest of us safe, healthy, alive and recovering from disease - to Tuesday, June 23,
2020, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of June 23, 2020

City Council Minutes  8  June 9, 2020
